evidence.claim: Silvermine takes its name from old legends of a silver mine, although no silver has ever been found.
evidence.quote: The name "Silvermine" comes from old legends of a silver mine in the area, although no silver has ever been found.

evidence.claim: The river supplied a more practical resource, powering twelve or thirteen mills in the eighteenth century, including tanning, lumber and spool works.
evidence.quote: In the eighteenth century, the Silvermine River was used for 12 or 13 mills in the neighborhood because it fell steeply enough for the water power to be profitably harnessed. The mills included a leather tanning works, sawmill, and spool works.

evidence.claim: In 1906, sculptor Solon Hannibal Borglum moved here and built a hillside studio.
evidence.quote: In 1906, Solon Hannibal Borglum, a sculptor, moved to the New Canaan part of Silvermine and built a hillside studio.

evidence.claim: Artists gathered there to critique one another’s work, calling themselves the Knockers Club.

evidence.claim: After Borglum’s death, the group founded the Silvermine Guild in 1922; the community remains home to the Silvermine Guild Arts Center.
